case_title: Ramesh and Others v. State of Haryana
previous_criminal_record: Not stated (only preventive proceedings under s.107/151 Cr.P.C. are mentioned; no criminal conviction is recorded)
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (Ramesh, husband); Relative (Suresh, brother-in-law; Saroj, sister-in-law; Prem, mother-in-law)
evidence_type: Dying declaration (recorded before a Magistrate, with doctor's fitness certificate); medical evidence (MLR and postmortem); hospital records; recovery of kerosene container; witness testimony
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged continuous dowry demands and physical torture; alleged prior attempt to drown the victim in a well
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of all charges (ss.302/34 and 498A/34 IPC)
high_court_outcome: Acquittal reversed; all four convicted. s.302/34 IPC: rigorous imprisonment for life and fine Rs.10,000 (default one year); s.498A/34 IPC: rigorous imprisonment for two years and fine Rs.2,000 (default six months)
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 read with s.34 IPC; cruelty to wife under s.498A read with s.34 IPC
neutral_facts: The victim had been married for about twenty years and had two adult sons. She was allegedly harassed over repeated dowry demands, including demands for a buffalo, money and a scooter, and was said to have been thrown into a well about a year earlier before villagers pulled her out. On the night of 19-20 September 1999 the victim was asleep in the matrimonial home when several family members came to her room. According to her later statement, two in-laws held her arms, another person poured kerosene over her, and a fourth lit a matchstick and set her ablaze. Neighbours extinguished the fire and the victim was taken to a hospital, where doctors found about 100% burn injuries. The attending doctor certified that she was fit to make a statement, and a Judicial Magistrate recorded her statement at the hospital in the doctor's presence. The doctor again recorded that she remained fit during the statement. The victim died within a few hours. The postmortem board found the burns were ante mortem and sufficient to cause death. Investigators registered an FIR on the statement, arrested the accused, and recovered a plastic kerosene container on the disclosure of one of them. At trial, the victim's father and brother did not support the prosecution account. The brother said one accused was with him at the time of the incident, but hospital records showed that accused had brought the victim to hospital.
offence_severity: Not stated (the judgment records only the sentence imposed for s.302/34 IPC: rigorous imprisonment for life and fine; no statutory maximum or minimum is stated)
physical_harm: Death of the victim from about 100% burn injuries within a few hours; postmortem found burns ante mortem and sufficient to cause death
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302 and s.498A, each with s.34); 2 finally upheld
motive: alleged: continuous dowry demands and harassment of the victim by in-laws
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration recorded by the Judicial Magistrate (PW-11) with the doctor's pre- and post-recording fitness endorsements; hospital records showing the husband brought the victim to hospital and had her admitted
witness_credibility: Magistrate (PW-11) credible; his cross-examination answer on semi-consciousness was read out of context. Brother (PW-4) discredited, as his alibi account was contradicted by hospital records. Father (PW-3) and brother (PW-4) turned hostile and were not believed; the court treated hostility as a product of compromise.
post_offence_conduct: The husband brought the victim to the hospital and had her admitted, as shown by hospital records; the court relied on this to discredit the brother's alibi testimony
trial_duration: offence: 20 September 1999; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 30 May 2014; Supreme Court: 22 November 2016
legal_representation: Accused: Praveen Kr. Aggarwal, Upendra Pratap Singh, Sanjay Jain (Advocates). State of Haryana: Jagdeep Kr. Sharma, Gyanendra Kr., Vishwa Pal Singh (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge sheet (s.173(2) report) filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Trial court did not consider the doctor's fitness opinion, did not examine whether precautions were taken before recording the dying declaration, and misread the Magistrate's evidence
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Court): acquitted. High Court: acquittal reversed, all four convicted. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, convictions upheld.
prosecution_argument: The incident took place in the matrimonial house; the deceased gave the statement after reaching hospital; the authorities were satisfied she was fit to give it, so the trial court wrongly discarded it
defence_argument: Acquittal should not be disturbed as two views were possible; the accused husband was with PW-4 on the night, showing false implication; a person with 100% burns could not give a statement, so the doctor's certificate should not be believed
legal_principle_applied: Appeal against acquittal: appellate court may reappreciate evidence but should not substitute its findings where trial court findings are equally plausible, unless perverse. Dying declaration admissible if the declarant was fit, voluntary and reliable; burn percentage alone is not decisive.
precedent_relied_upon: Sanwat Singh v. State of Rajasthan 1961 SCR (3) 120; Govindaraju @ Govinda v. State by Sriramapuram Police Station (2012) 4 SCC 722; Jai Karan v. State of N.C.T., Delhi (1999) 8 SCC 161; Rambai v. State of Chhattisgarh (2002) 8 SCC 83; Kushal Rao v. State of Bombay 1958 SCR 552; Vikas v. State of Maharashtra (2008) 2 SCC 516; Krishna Mochi (2002) 6 SCC 81; Zahira Habibullah (2006) 3 SCC 374; Sakshi (2004) 5 SCC 518; State v. Sanjeev Nanda (2012) 8 SCC 450
